Article Title: BSP's family drama: Why no 'Anand' for Mayawati ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections?
Article Text:
Mayawati said Akash Anand, the BSP's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. (File Photo)

FIL bends but Mayawati refuses to budge

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

Third time unlucky?

Anand's FIL connection and maturity question

Can BSP afford this 'family drama'?

NEW DELHI: Three promotions. Three demotions. And now staring at a possible exit!Well, that’s how the political scorecard reads for Akash Anand, whose “maturity meter” has not just failed him again, but has also put him on the brink of exit from the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).7 days after his third demotion, Akash Anand finds himself in a difficult spot, with BSP chief Mayawati opening the doors for his exit from the party. "The people in the party feel that just as he was relieved of all the important responsibilities of the post of national coordinator on September 3, 2026, he should now also be completely freed from the party from today. Therefore, if Akash Anand wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so; that is, he has now been completely freed from the party," Mayawati posted on X.This despite the fact that Akash Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth on Thursday bowed before Mayawati's ultimatum and announced his retirement from politics and social life, after the BSP chief linked his "sanyas" to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew Akash Anand.In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.But neither Siddharth's actions nor his words made any impact on Mayawati.She questioned Siddharth's intentions, saying his "announcement should have come immediately after her call for him to retire." Mayawati alleged that the delay showed that Siddharth's ambitions and intentions had not changed completely."If Ashok Siddharth had even a little genuine concern for the bright future of his son-in-law Akash Anand and the larger interests of the BSP and its Ambedkarite Bahujan movement, he would have announced his retirement without delay," she said.Mayawati also slammed Anand for not reposting her earlier X post linking his future responsibilities in the party to his father-in-law's retirement. She said Anand had earlier reposted posts from her social media account "to demonstrate his loyalty," but had not done so in this case despite the post being in his own interest.Mayawati said this indicated that both Siddharth and Anand were more attached to personal and family interests than to the success of the party and its movement.She questioned whether Anand could effectively serve the BSP while remaining caught between his family ties and the interests of the party."If Akash Anand is less concerned about the real interests of the party and the movement and his own political career, and more attached to family relationships, then it is natural to ask how he can work for the good of the BSP and the movement while remaining double-minded," she said.Akash Anand’s latest demotion was on September 3, when aunt Mayawati announced that her nephew had again lost his political maturity."I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party," Mayawati said at a national-level meeting of BSP office-bearers.And that ensured Akash Anand, the chief national coordinator of BSP, was back to square one. His Twitter bio reflected the sudden change in his status within the party. From BSP "National Convenor", he became "Party Worker, BSP." Just a few days later, he made yet another edit to his bio, which read: "Party Supporter, BSP." This is how his X bio reads now.It was less than a month back, August 10 to be exact, that Akash Anand had formally launched the BSP’s election campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections from Sadabad assembly constituency in Hathras. He addressed a well-attended rally and launched a broadside against the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over jobs, education and law and order, while taking digs at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, calling them both “uncle. ”From being anointed Mayawati’s successor to being a party worker and now a party supporter - it has been a tumultuous and bumpy ride for the young Akash Anand. And this time around there is a twist in the tale: Akash’s younger brother Ishan Anand has been brought to the centre stage.On September 3, when Mayawati entered the venue of the meeting of office-bearers, walking behind her was not Akash but his younger brother Ishan. Wearing the BSP's blue sash around his neck, he stood behind his aunt till she settled down.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSP’s national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.After 6 days of suspense, Mayawati finally revealed what triggered her against Akash Anand yet again. In a long post on X, Mayawati explained how Akash Anand had once again, after two years, lost his “political maturity.” And also, what he could do to get it back.The trigger this time around was Ashok Siddharth, the father in law of Akash Anand. Ashok Siddharth was expelled by Maywati from BSP last month for the second time over indiscipline and anti-party stance.Taking to X, the BSP supremo wrote: “It is well known that Ashok Siddharth had previously been expelled for indiscipline and violating guidelines, specifically regarding the distribution of party tickets and a failure to coordinate properly with BSP Maharashtra state president during state elections. He had been reinstated on the condition that he would not repeat such mistakes and would be assigned responsibility of expanding the party's support base only in other states, not in Uttar Pradesh. ”She also informed that Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the party “under any circumstances in the future”.Hardening her stand further against Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati stated that a clear path remains for Akash Anand to resume an active leadership role within the movement, provided Siddharth steps aside completely."In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc., and completely retire from politics. Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the party—this is the general consensus in the party," Mayawati said in her post.Urging people from the Dalit community, to not engage in any action driven by personal or familial interests that creates obstacles in their path, for which “history may not forgive them," Mayawati cited Ashok Siddharth as a prime example of an official prioritising "personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, despite receiving multiple opportunities to reform."The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," Mayawati said in her statement.With the UP assembly elections just months away, a family drama is the last thing that the BSP cadres in the state would have hoped for. The party’s trajectory in the state has been downhill. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawati’s dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her party’s vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSP’s influence among Dalits.From a sweeping majority in 2007 to allegations of being the B-team of BJP, the BSP’s political fortunes have nosedived in the state. The BSP supporters have dwindled and some have even changed loyalties, but what remains still strong is Mayawati’s appeal and popularity among the party’s cadres.However, the 2027 challenge is going to be tough for Maywati and her BSP. The SP-Congress alliance managed to garner a lot of Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, upsetting BJP’s applecart in the state and eventually at the Centre. Cleary this was not the time when the BSP chief should have precipitated action against Akash Anand and pitched one nephew against the other.Mayawati needs a strong comeback and to ensure that she has to first set her house in order. All the more, as she has announced that BSP will not enter into any alliance in future elections. The BSP needs to perform if Mayawati wants to remain relevant in the state’s politics. Another poor show where she wins votes but not seats will reinforce allegations that BSP is the B-team of the BJP.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national coordinator Akash Anand on brink of exit. BSP chief Mayawati opens doors for his exit from the party. Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth, announces his retirement.

Article Title: How BJP, Congress turned 80s AI trend turned into an all-out meme war
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's original picture from the 80s. Rahul Gandhi's (R) AI-generated image.

What is the trend?

NEW DELHI: What began as another harmless social media trend, turning present-day photographs into portraits straight out of the 1980s, has now found its way into the social feeds of politicians has triggered BJP-Congress war of memes.Over the past few days, Instagram and X have been flooded with AI-generated photographs featuring big hair, aviator sunglasses, denim jackets, vintage suits and the grainy finish of old family albums.BJP leaders were among the first to jump onto the trend. Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal shared an AI-generated photograph of himself dressed in a grey suit and aviators, writing simply: "Vibing to the 80s trend."Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed with his own retro look, posing beside a car in an image designed to resemble a photograph from the decade."Why is everyone going back to the 80s vibes? I'm also forced to 80s nostalgia!" he wrote.Congress Sevadal brought Rahul Gandhi into the picture, posting AI-generated photographs of the leader of opposition with the caption: "Rahul Gandhi catches the 80s trend wave."The BJP's official X handle also shared some original pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi believed to be from the 1980s era.What started as politicians recreating their younger selves soon became another format for the BJP and Congress to take veiled potshots at each other with AI doing the set design.The Congress's Kerala unit shared an AI-generated image showing a bald man sitting in the front passenger seat of a Maruti Suzuki Omni, with the caption: "A Gujarat street in the 80s."For context, the van, launched in India in the 1980s, became a familiar sight in Bollywood films where it was often shown being used by goons and kidnappers, eventually earning its own "kidnapping van" meme identity.BJP Gujarat hit back with an AI-generated image of its own.BJP's Telangana unit also responded to the Congress post. It shared an image showing a woman in a red dress dancing on a table inside what appeared to be a bar, with liquor bottles visible in cabinets behind her.The description read: "Lusiana, Italy. Circa-1970s."The BJP did not name anyone in the post either, but the reference was widely seen as an allusion to Lusiana, the Italian town where former Congress president Sonia Gandhi was born.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor , however, found a way of joining the trend without asking AI to take him back in time."The 1980s seem to be back, courtesy of AI. I thought I’d join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, sharing photographs that were actually taken during the decade.The pictures included Tharoor with his sons Ishaan and Kanishk.The trend itself is simple. Users upload a present-day selfie to AI tools such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini and ask them to recreate the image as if it had been taken in the 1980s.Unlike a regular vintage filter, the AI rebuilds the photograph around the person’s face, adding everything from big hairstyles and retro clothes to film grain and old-school studio lighting.The result is a polished throwback image that looks straight out of an old photo album or Bollywood publicity still. The trend has spread rapidly across Instagram and X, with influencers, celebrities and now politicians joining in.
Article Summary: AI-generated images of present-day selfies are being turned into portraits straight out of the 1980s. BJP leaders were among the first to jump onto the trend. The BJP's official X handle also shared some original pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: Recent Brics summits didn't benefit India, says PC; BJP hits back
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP and Congress sparred ahead of the Brics summit as P Chidambaram questioned if its last few meetings have brought India any tangible benefits, comments slammed by Nitin Nabin as familiar whining by the opposition over the country's rise and growth."World is looking at India but comments being made by Congress members are shameful. Rahul Gandhi and Congress netas have been insulting India on foreign soil. Now when India is hosting a big international event, they are again pained," the BJP chief told reporters.These "naraz fufas", a barb PM Modi has used to dismiss criticism from Congress netas, were similarly hurt when India hosted G20 and AI summits, Nabin said. His remarks came after Chidambaram told a news agency, "I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results. In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20 and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, Brics summits resulted in tangible benefits."BJP spokesman Sudhanshu Trivedi mocked Chidambaram, saying that when so many world leaders are coming to India for the summit, he seems to place his wisdom above theirs.
Article Summary: P Chidambaram questioned if last few meetings have brought India any tangible benefits. Comments slammed by Nitin Nabin as familiar whining by the opposition over the country's rise and growth. These "naraz fufas" were similarly hurt when India hosted G20 and AI summits, Nabin said.

Article Title: TN minister reiterates Rahul Gandhi for PM pitch; rules out Vijay as contender
Article Text:
Leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi

Rahul Gandhi remains Congress’ choice

Vijay’s PM pitch dismissed

Congress hopes Left will join alliance

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister and Congress leader P Viswanathan on Thursday reiterated that Rahul Gandhi will be the party’s Prime Ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, saying he would also be projected as the INDIA bloc’s candidate.Viswanathan made the remarks while speaking to reporters at Tiruchirappalli International Airport, where he arrived from Chennai en route to Thiruvarur to attend various programmes.Asked who would be the Prime Ministerial candidate of the INDIA bloc, Viswanathan said there was “no hesitation” in stating the Congress’ position, news agency ANI reported.“I am a Congressperson by birth. Our clear position is that Rahul Gandhi should be the Prime Ministerial candidate. Rahul Gandhi will be chosen as the Prime Ministerial candidate of the INDIA bloc,” he said.Responding to a question about Congress MP Manickam Tagore allegedly being hesitant to name Rahul Gandhi as the PM candidate, Viswanathan said, “As a Congress minister, I openly declare that Rahul Gandhi is our Prime Ministerial candidate for 2029.”Viswanathan also rejected suggestions that Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Vijay could be projected as the Opposition’s Prime Ministerial candidate.He said it was natural for every political party to project its own leader and there was nothing wrong with the Congress putting forward Rahul Gandhi, given the party’s long political history.Viswanathan said the assessment that Vijay could be projected as the PM candidate was incorrect and suggested that Vijay himself could announce Rahul Gandhi’s name. He, however, said it was too early to discuss the issue.Praising Rahul Gandhi’s political journey, Viswanathan said his struggles should be “engraved in golden letters in world history”.The minister also said the Congress was working with the confidence that the Left parties would join its alliance.His remarks came a day after the TVK-led ruling alliance formally adopted the name “Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance” at a meeting of its constituent parties at the TVK headquarters in Panaiyur.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister and Congress leader P Viswanathan reiterated that Rahul Gandhi will be the party’s Prime Ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He also rejected suggestions that Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Vijay could be projected.

Article Title: “We are beyond thankful for everyone’s support”: How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned Team 62 into a $3.69M legacy for the autism community
Article Text:
How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned Team 62 into a $3.69M legacy for the autism communityImage credit (Instagram)

How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned Team 62 into a growing tradition

How Team 62 became part of the Kelces’ lasting Eagles legacy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason and Kylie Kelce have turned a summer charity event into something much bigger than a yearly fundraiser. Since Team 62 began in 2021, the event has brought Eagles fans, families and members of the autism community together while creating another major source of support for the Eagles Autism Foundation.The sixth annual Team 62 fundraiser continued that growth in 2026. Held on June 24 in Sea Isle City, the event raised more than $1.26 million in a single night, taking the total raised through the fundraiser since 2021 beyond $3.69 million. What started as a local community event has steadily become one of the most recognizable charitable weekends connected to the Eagles and the Kelce family.The success of Team 62 has never depended only on one evening. Jason and Kylie have helped build an entire weekend around the cause, giving people different ways to participate while keeping the focus on the autism community.The 2026 weekend included an all-abilities football clinic, a cheerleading clinic and an Eagles drumline workshop. Families could also take part in beach yoga and other activities in Sea Isle City. The mix of events helped make the weekend more inclusive, allowing people of different abilities and ages to join in rather than making the fundraiser feel like a traditional celebrity charity event.The main fundraiser at Ocean Drive brought together current and former Eagles players, Eagles cheerleaders, mascot SWOOP and members of the Kelce family, including Donna Kelce. Guests could support the cause through tips, raffles, merchandise purchases and other donations.Jason and Kylie later shared their appreciation for everyone who helped make the latest event such a success. “We are beyond thankful for everyone’s support and generosity in setting a Team 62 fundraising record,” they said.The fundraising continued beyond Ocean Drive, too. The fourth annual Beer Bowl at the Sea Isle City Yacht Club, an online auction and entry fees from other community activities all contributed to the weekend's total. Together, those efforts helped the sixth Team 62 fundraiser raise more than $1.26 million.Jason Kelce’s connection with Philadelphia has always gone beyond what happened on the football field. He spent his entire NFL career with the Eagles, became one of the most recognizable players in franchise history and remained closely connected with the city following his retirement. Team 62 has given him and Kylie another way to maintain that connection while supporting a cause that reaches far beyond football.The Eagles Autism Foundation has also recognized the role the couple has played in growing the fundraiser. Executive Director Ryan Hammond praised Jason and Kylie as outstanding ambassadors for the foundation, pointing to their passion and creative approach as reasons Team 62 has become such an important annual event.For the Kelces, however, the latest record was never presented as their achievement alone. They credited the Eagles organization, Sea Isle City and the supporters who continue to return each year.“Six years later, we now stand here amazed at what we’ve accomplished for the autism community,” Jason and Kylie said. They also gave a special thank-you to the Eagles organization, the town of Sea Isle City and “the best fans in the world” for continuing to support the cause.With more than $3.69 million raised since 2021, Team 62 has clearly grown beyond its beginnings. The $1.26 million night added another major chapter, but the lasting part of the Kelces’ work may be the community they have created around the fundraiser, giving families a welcoming place to come together while supporting the Eagles Autism Foundation year after year.
Article Summary: The sixth annual Team 62 fundraiser continued that growth in 2026. Held on June 24 in Sea Isle City, the event raised more than $1.26 million in a single night. The total raised through the fundraiser since 2021 beyond $3.69 million.

Article Title: ‘He is not being neglected’: Sourav Ganguly’s blunt verdict on Mohammed Shami
Article Text:
Mohammed Shami (PTI Photo)

Ganguly backs Ishan Kishan for Test return

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sourav Ganguly has rejected the suggestion that Mohammed Shami is being overlooked by India's selectors, saying the veteran pacer has already achieved plenty and remains “an absolute champion”. Shami has not played for India since the Champions Trophy 2025, where he was an important part of the side that won the title. The 36-year-old has continued to feature in domestic cricket during his absence from the national team and on Thursday helped East Zone end a 13-year wait for the Duleep Trophy.Ganguly, speaking to reporters at the Eden Gardens, said Shami's continued commitment to domestic cricket and his performances were particularly encouraging.“What makes me happy for Shami is that he turns out day in and day out in domestic cricket and performs. It is terrific to see. He has achieved so much," Ganguly said.With Shami still producing performances in domestic cricket, Ganguly was asked whether the pacer could force his way back into India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup.The former India captain, however, felt it was far too early to make such a prediction, pointing out that the tournament is still some distance away.“That's a long way. I can't comment. It's in October (next year). It's a long way," he said.Ganguly was also asked whether he believed Shami was being neglected by the senior men's selection panel.He strongly disagreed, while acknowledging that being left out can become part of a cricketer's career as age advances. Ganguly drew on his own experience of being dropped from India's World Cup plans despite having already crossed the 10,000-run mark in international cricket.“He is not being neglected. He has played a lot. He is an absolute champion. But as you grow older, this happens. When I got left out from World Cup one-day cricket for a year, after scoring 10,000 runs, I found my way to come back. So this happens with everyone.”The comments came on a day when Ganguly also congratulated East Zone on their Duleep Trophy triumph, which ended a long wait for the title.Ganguly also had words of praise for East Zone captain Ishan Kishan, whose performances in the Duleep Trophy have strengthened his case for a possible return to India's Test side.The CAB president revealed that he had spoken to Kishan on Thursday and backed the wicketkeeper-batter to keep targeting Test cricket.“I spoke to Kishan this afternoon. It's terrific and remarkable. Every young player wants to play Test cricket, and hopefully he will. He played exceptionally well in all the finals of the Vijay Hazare, Syed Mushtaq Ali, and Duleep Trophy.”Ganguly stressed the importance of Test cricket for young players and highlighted Kishan's ability to produce runs when the stakes are highest.“If he performs, I think for every young player Test cricket should be important. They must want to play Test cricket and hopefully he will. He gets runs in big matches.... Vijay Hazare final, Mushtaq final, Duleep Trophy final.”Kishan's last Test appearance for India came against the West Indies in July 2023. Since then, he has been working his way back into contention, and his latest run of performances has given his Test ambitions another boost.
Article Summary: Sourav Ganguly says Mohammed Shami is not being neglected by India selectors. Ganguly also backs Ishan Kishan for a possible return to India's Test side. Former India captain also congratulates East Zone on their Duleep Trophy triumph.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $300,000 cancer donation and $80 million orphanage claim sparked heavy controversy
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce donation rumor fails to hold up

Travis Kelce has previously warned about AI charity stories

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new viral story involving Travis Kelce has been exposed as false, after social media posts claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star and his fiancée had spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on a child battling brain cancer. The same posts also tied Kelce to an alleged $80 million orphanage project. However, no credible evidence supports either claim, with the story appearing to be another example of AI-generated celebrity misinformation.The claim began circulating on Facebook in late November, packaged as a dramatic breaking-news story about Kelce and his charitable efforts. Posts alleged that the NFL tight end and his fiancée had paid $300,000 toward medical treatment for a 2-year-old child with brain cancer.The story then went much further. It claimed the couple planned to spend $80 million building what was described as the largest free orphanage in the United States.For Kelce, the rumor is notable because it follows a growing pattern of fabricated stories that attach his name to emotional charity cases. The posts used images designed to make the claims look convincing, including pictures of Kelce and his fiancée alongside a hospitalized toddler and a building carrying a sign that read "Taylor Swift Orphanage."A closer look, however, found no credible news reports confirming the alleged $300,000 donation or the orphanage plan. The websites spreading the claim also appeared to be designed to attract clicks and advertising revenue.That matters because the story was not simply an unverified social media post. It was presented with the tone and appearance of a major charitable announcement, encouraging readers to accept an extraordinary claim before checking its source.The latest rumor also fits with an issue Kelce has addressed before. In April 2025, he responded on his "New Heights with Jason & Travis Kelce" podcast to another false claim about his charitable activities.While discussing the spread of fabricated stories, Kelce said, "This time I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or the outlets posting all this AI stuff."He also pointed audiences toward 87running.org, the website for his foundation, as a place to find authentic information about his charitable work.There is an important distinction behind the latest rumor. A real story reported in October 2025 said that his fiancée donated $100,000 to help the family of a 2-year-old child battling brain cancer. That genuine act may have provided the seed for the much larger fabricated claim involving Kelce, $300,000 and an $80 million orphanage.Kelce has also been involved in legitimate charitable work, making it easier for false stories to appear believable when they use his name. But the absence of reliable reporting is a major warning sign.The episode is another reminder that emotional celebrity stories can travel quickly online, especially when they involve children, illness and huge donations. For readers, checking the original source and looking for confirmation from established news organizations remains one of the simplest ways to separate genuine philanthropy from an AI-generated viral rumor.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce and his fiancée allegedly spent $300,000 on a 2-year-old child with brain cancer. Posts also tied Kelce to an alleged $80 million orphanage project. No credible evidence supports either claim, making it another example of AI- generated celebrity misinformation.

Article Title: 'He made us all believe': How Dhoni is quietly shaping Jharkhand's next generation
Article Text:
Image credit: Agencies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Mahendra Singh Dhoni ’s influence on Jharkhand cricket has never needed an official designation. Even after stepping away from the domestic cricket long ago, the former India captain continues to leave his imprint quietly, helping shape a young generation that is now beginning to make its presence felt at the highest domestic level across formats.East Zone’s Duleep Trophy triumph on Thursday, their first since 2012, offered perhaps the clearest indication yet of the strength of Jharkhand’s emerging batting core. Captain Ishan Kishan led from the front, aggregating 350 runs in the final, while Shikhar Mohan, Kumar Kushagra, Md Kounain Quraishi and Anukul Roy were among the Jharkhand players who made significant contributions during the campaign.The title, naturally, was a collective East Zone achievement. Bengal supplied considerable experience through Mohammed Shami, Mukesh Kumar, Abhimanyu Easwaran, Sudip Gharami and Shahbaz Ahmed, while Bihar’s teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also made his mark in the semifinal with the fastest half-century in the history of the tournament. But the performance of Jharkhand’s young middle-order batters provided one of the strongest threads running through East Zone’s campaign.And behind that progression, there is a familiar figure who continues to offer guidance without occupying any formal role.“Whenever he is free and in Ranchi, he visits the (JSCA) stadium. From juniors to seniors, when camps are going on, he comes himself, talks to people and gets involved. When we won Mushtaq Ali last year, the first congratulatory message I received was by Mahi bhai,” JSCA secretary and former India and Jharkhand batter Saurabh Tiwary said of Dhoni.“He keeps telling us which players are good and should be watched. He also speaks to players whenever they get an opportunity to meet him and tells them how to perform. The most important thing he discusses with them is how to read the game. That is a huge mental factor when you are playing at the top level,” Tiwary told TOI on Thursday.Once a regular in the Indian Premier League, Tiwary said Dhoni’s involvement has grown significantly and that his interest in the state setup remains remarkably close. Dhoni can, according to Tiwary, “name Jharkhand’s playing XI any day and keeps a close watch on emerging players”.That influence is not necessarily about technical instruction. It is about understanding what it takes to survive and succeed at the top level — something Dhoni knows better than most.Former Jharkhand player Ishank Jaggi and now their U-23 coach, who has also worked closely with several of the state’s younger cricketers, believes the current crop has developed a greater understanding of their game.“MSD was the first guy playing for the country from Jharkhand. He made us all believe that players from Jharkhand can also be at the top level,” Jaggi said.According to Jaggi, the Player of the Match in the 2012 Duleep Trophy final – the last time East Zone was triumphant – Dhoni remains closely connected with the state’s cricket ecosystem despite his busy schedule.“Whenever he is in Ranchi and free, he makes sure he is at the (JSCA) stadium. Coaches and players ask him about different situations and he shares his experiences. Whether it’s the men’s team or the women’s team, everybody benefits from his inputs.”Jaggi also believes the likes of Kushagra and Mohan are capable of pushing for India selection. Shikhar, in particular, has emerged as one of Jharkhand’s most promising all-round young cricketers, with his batting, bowling and fielding across formats drawing praise from Tiwary.“I think in the coming three years you will see even more good players coming through,” Tiwary said. “The future looks very good for Jharkhand.”That optimism is rooted in more than one successful Duleep Trophy campaign and their maiden Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy triumph last year under Kishan and with same set-up. Tiwary pointed to a growing system in which former players are now involved in coaching, selection and administration, bringing with them a close understanding of the players and the pathway they have travelled.For a generation that grew up idolising Dhoni, he remains the most influential link between Jharkhand’s cricketing past and its future and East Zone’s Duleep Trophy triumph offered a glimpse of what may lie ahead. The likes of Kishan, Kushagra, Shikhar, Roy and Quraishi are already making their mark beyond state cricket as Jharkhand’s former players continue to mentor the next batch, backed by Dhoni’s quiet but enduring guidance.
Article Summary: East Zone win Duleep Trophy for first time since 2012. Captain Ishan Kishan led from the front, aggregating 350 runs in the final. Shikhar Mohan, Kumar Kushagra, Md Kounain Quraishi and Anukul Roy were among the Jharkhand players who made significant contributions.

Article Title: ‘My name was not even in the FIR’: How a former India cricketer's 22-year ordeal ended in acquittal after a controversial UK tour, arrest and Tihar Jail
Article Text:
Jacob Martin

From Ranji runs to the India cap

jacob martin

The tour that changed everything

Arrest, Tihar and a career quietly dismantled

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the pressure athletes face from public scrutiny during legal issues? It is too much pressure It’s part of their life in the spotlight 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For most cricketers, the innings that define them are played out in the middle. Jacob Martin's longest battle was fought in a courtroom.The former India batsman was acquitted in a 22-year-old criminal case tied to a controversial 2004 cricket tour of the United Kingdom. The Patiala House Court in Delhi cleared the Vadodara resident of all charges: forgery, cheating, criminal conspiracy and offences under the Passport Act.The case traced back to a 2004 FIR invoking Sections 420, 468, 471 and 120B of the IPC alongside Section 12 of the Passport Act. Prosecutors alleged a forged UK immigration stamp, dubious travel arrangements and financial transactions involving Martin. None of it held up.Nor did the court find credible evidence of Martin owning or controlling Ajwa Sports Club, the club at the centre of the allegations. Witness after witness failed to back the prosecution's case, and the charges collapsed.Martin is 54 now. The verdict closes a chapter that ran for more than two decades and reshaped both his career and his life outside it.Before any of this, Martin had built a name as one of domestic cricket's most reliable middle-order batsmen. Born in Baroda, he made his living on concentration and the sheer willingness to bat time. His breakout came in the 1998-99 Ranji Trophy , when he crossed 1,000 runs for the season and became only the sixth batter in the competition's history to do so.That run brought him national attention, and eventually a India call-up.His first-class career dwarfs his international one. Martin played 138 first-class matches, scored over 9,000 runs, hit 23 centuries and averaged above 46. He also captained Baroda to the 2000-01 Ranji Trophy, still the team's most recent title, and later returned to Baroda cricket as a coach.At the international level, though, it never really took off. Ten ODIs, a debut against the West Indies in Toronto in 1999, and a stretch between 1999 and 2001 in which he managed 158 runs at 22.57.The number that shadows Martin's career isn't 10 caps or 9,000 first-class runs. It's 22, the years the case hung over him.By his account, it started with a team associated with him that travelled to the UK in 2004. Most of the players came home. One didn't, overstaying his six-month visa. That player, Martin says, arranged a fake immigration stamp through a contact in Britain. He was eventually deported and picked up at Indira Gandhi International Airport for questioning.Martin insists his name wasn't in the original FIR at all, that he was pulled into the investigation later, partly because of who he was."In 2004 a team of mine had gone, which had gone to the UK to play. That team which went to play in England in 2004, everyone came back except one boy who stayed back in the UK. Because the visa had a validity of 6 months, he could stay for 6 months, but he overstayed for more than 6 months, so what happened was that he got fake stamping done there through someone. After getting fake stamping done, when he came back to India, he was deported from the UK, so he was caught at the IGI airport, and then he was questioned," Martin said.Police told a different story. They alleged Martin and an associate had arranged the boy's trip under the pretence of a cricket tour, with money involved, and that Ajwa Sports Club, described as a bogus outfit, was used in the arrangement. There was even a suggestion of human trafficking or an illegal-immigration racket.None of it stood up in court.Martin was arrested in Delhi and spent time in Tihar Jail while the case crawled through the system.It still hadn't been resolved by 2016, when the Baroda Cricket Association named him Ranji Trophy coach, a decision that drew criticism given that the case was still pending.Away from the field, the damage was more direct. Martin says he lost his job with the Railways over the case and could never get a foothold with the BCCI . Two decades of uncertainty took their toll."My name was not even in the FIR, but when the investigation took place, I was involved in this case because the name was big and I was an international cricketer, because of that. And after the case ended, this... now, after 22 years... during these 22 years, I was not getting any answers from the BCCI either; I lost my job in the railways. So I had a lot of stress because of this, but this judgment that has come now- I have got a clean chit; it will be a big settlement for my life and very. .. after 22 years, this... appeal I have received is a very big U-turn for my life," he added.The court case wasn't the only thing testing him. In December 2018, Martin was badly injured in a road accident in Vadodara, with his lung and liver both damaged. He was put on a ventilator, spent nearly a month in intensive care, and for a while his condition was critical.Former teammates and administrators rallied to help cover his treatment.More than two decades after that tour to England, Martin's legal ordeal has ended. It won't undo the years he lost. But it gives him something he hadn't had in a long while: a life after cricket that isn't defined by a case still hanging over him.
Article Summary: Former India batsman Jacob Martin was acquitted in a 22-year-old criminal case tied to a controversial 2004 cricket tour of the UK. Martin played 138 first- class matches, scored over 9,000 runs, hit 23 centuries and averaged above 46. He captained Baroda to the 2000-01 Ranji Trophy, still the team's most recent title.

Article Title: Inspiring story on fatherhood:“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had”- How LeBron James turned pain into a promise
Article Text:
LeBron James’ fatherhood began with a promise

Akron Beacon Journal

LeBron James learned fatherhood without a manual

Vogue

The Shop

LeBron James admits the NBA took time away from his children

LeBron James’ children became part of his greatest achievement

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At 19, LeBron James was already carrying the weight of an NBA franchise when fatherhood gave him an entirely different responsibility. His first son, Bronny, was born in October 2004, just months after James entered the league as the No. 1 overall pick. More than two decades later, his early promise to become a better father still offers a revealing look at the man behind the basketball legend.The quote that best captures LeBron James’ approach to fatherhood came at a defining moment in his young life. According to contemporary reports, James spoke to thearound the time his first child was born in October 2004.His words were simple, but the reason behind them was deeply personal.“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had,” James told the newspaper. “I didn’t know him. I didn’t know the situation he was in. But I’m going to do my job the best way I can. I’m excited about it. It’s a wonderful opportunity in life.”James had grown up primarily with his mother, Gloria, without his biological father playing a meaningful role in his childhood. Becoming a father himself therefore meant more than welcoming a baby.It gave him a chance to build the kind of family relationship he had never experienced.The timing made the moment even more striking. James was only 19, preparing for his second NBA season and learning how to handle the expectations that came with being the league's most celebrated young player.His life was moving at an extraordinary pace. Basketball demanded nearly everything from him, yet fatherhood gave him a reason to think beyond the next game, season or championship.As his family grew, James repeatedly acknowledged that parenting did not come with a perfect formula.In a 2017interview, he explained that there was no definitive guide for raising children because every child and family situation was different. He also credited Savannah James with taking the lead at home while his NBA career kept him on the road.That reality became particularly important as James and Savannah raised Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.Years earlier, James had made a similar point during a CNN interview with Rachel Nichols. Asked about guiding his children, he stressed that parents can provide values and direction, but ultimately children must learn to make their own decisions.His philosophy was not to dictate every move. It was to prepare his children for the moments when he would not be there to make the decision for them.That approach also shaped the way he viewed his sons' basketball careers. James knew better than most that having an NBA superstar as a father could create enormous expectations.In 2018, while discussing Bronny on, James admitted that he regretted giving his son his name because of the pressure that could follow him. He explained that his original motivation came from his own childhood and his desire to do things differently.“The only thing I can do is give them the blueprint, and it’s up to them to take their own course whenever that time comes.”That line reveals another important part of James' parenting style. He could offer experience, protection and advice, but he could not live his children's lives for them.For all the success James achieved, fatherhood also forced him to confront a painful cost of professional sports: time.After eventually sharing an NBA court with Bronny, James reflected on the years he had spent travelling and playing.“It’s family. It’s always been family over everything,” James said, acknowledging that his career had meant missing moments involving Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.That admission adds another layer to his early promise.Being a better father was never simply about providing financially. James understood that being present mattered too. NBA seasons are long. Travel is constant. Even the most successful athlete cannot recover every birthday, school event or ordinary family evening lost to work.His comments over the years suggest that this tension has stayed with him.Yet basketball also produced moments that made the sacrifices feel worthwhile.When Bronny joined the Los Angeles Lakers, James became the first father to play alongside his son in an NBA regular-season game. The historic moment arrived on Oct. 22, 2024, when the two checked into the Lakers' game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.For James, the achievement carried an emotional meaning that went beyond basketball.The teenager who had once promised to become a better father than the one he had was now sharing an NBA floor with his own son.James has never suggested that being a father is easy. Instead, his comments show how much he has learned while raising three children under extraordinary public attention.In 2016, he told ESPN that one of his favorite parts of fatherhood was watching his children grow and recognizing pieces of his younger self in them.That may be one of the most human parts of his story. The NBA superstar who spends his career being judged by statistics and championships also has to deal with the ordinary emotions of parenthood.He gets proud. He worries. He gives advice. He sometimes sees his younger self in his children.And he has had to learn when to step in and when to let them find their own way.That balance became even more meaningful after Bronny suffered cardiac arrest during a workout at USC in July 2023. James later said he would dedicate the following season to his son, adding, “Understanding that puts everything in perspective.”The episode reminded James and his family that careers, records and championships can suddenly become secondary.His fatherhood journey has therefore come full circle in a way that few could have predicted when he was 19. He entered adulthood without the relationship with his own father that many children take for granted. He then became a father himself while carrying the expectations of an entire basketball city.Instead of allowing that absence to define him, James turned it into a standard for himself.The exact viral quote about giving his children everything he did not have should not be attributed to him. His documented words are arguably more powerful anyway.“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had.”More than 20 years later, his career shows how seriously he took that promise.
Article Summary: At 19, LeBron James was already carrying the weight of an NBA franchise. His first son, Bronny, was born in October 2004, just months after James entered the league as the No. 1 overall pick. James' early promise to become a better father still offers a revealing look at him.

Article Title: 'Embarrassing': Wasim Akram slams Pakistan's shocking mid-tour changes
Article Text:

‘Give the system four to five years’

Former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram has criticised the major changes made to the team in the middle of its England tour, calling the situation “embarrassing” and pointing to a lack of communication within the setup.Akram said Pakistan need more consistency and better communication if they want to improve their performances.“Consistency is the key, of course, but for how long? When seven players and two coaches return in the middle of a tour, it is embarrassing for the team and the captain, and it also shows there is a lack of communication,” Akram said while speaking to YouTuber Furqan Bhatti.Akram believes Pakistan still have enough talent to compete at the highest level. He said his experience with Pakistan Super League (PSL) teams has given him a close look at the country’s players.“I have been involved in the PSL with these teams for the past four to five years, so I have seen the situation closely. In my view, the talent is there. Coaches may change, but the core players remain largely the same,” he said.The former Pakistan captain also asked the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to give the domestic system enough time to produce results instead of making regular changes.“Everyone has to give the system at least three to four years.Whoever comes in next should avoid constantly changing the first-class structure. Give it four to five years, and then you will see the results,” he said.Akram also stressed the need to strengthen cricket at the grassroots level. He called for greater focus on club, school and college cricket to ensure a steady supply of talent.“We need to revive club cricket as well as school and college cricket. If grassroots cricket disappears, where will the talent come from? The PCB only takes players after they reach a certain stage,” Akram added.Meanwhile, Pakistan’s problems on the England tour continued at Edgbaston as Ollie Robinson struck twice in his opening over on Thursday.Robinson, man of the match in the first two Tests, took a wicket with the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings and struck again three deliveries later.Pakistan reached 52-2 before rain brought an early end to play on day two. They still needed 268 runs to make England bat again.

Calls for greater focus on club, school and college cricket to ensure a steady supply of talent. Pakistan reached 52-2 before rain brought an early end to play on day two.

Article Title: "I’m too scared": Angel Reese makes a bold promise about her love life and fans may have to wait for a ring
Article Text:
Angel Reese explains why her dating life stays private

Unapologetically Angel

Unapologetically Angel

Angel Reese has drawn a firm line between her public career and her private life. The Chicago Sky star has made it clear that fans should not expect regular relationship updates from her social media accounts. Reese explained that the intense attention surrounding her dating life changed the way she views romance in the public eye, leading her to make one striking promise about what she will share next.Reese opened up about her approach to relationships during an episode of her podcastin 2024. At the time, she was speaking with stylist Law Roach when the conversation turned toward dating and the pressure that can come with being a highly visible athlete.The topic was especially relevant for Reese. At 6-foot-4, she is already one of the most recognizable players in the WNBA, and her life away from basketball often attracts almost as much attention as what happens on the court.She admitted that she was unsure whether she would date someone shorter than her, even though she did not completely rule it out.“I don’t know. I’m too scared,” Reese said when discussing the possibility.But her biggest message was not about height. It was about privacy.Reese had previously addressed the issue on social media after her dating life became a subject of intense online discussion. Her frustration was clear.“Now i see why people hide relationships & keep everything private 😭 like i don’t think i’ll ever openly share that part of my life with yall again until im married cause yall do THE MOST!”The post reflected a growing divide between what Reese was willing to share with fans and what she wanted to keep for herself. For someone whose professional life is constantly dissected, a private relationship offered a rare space where she could simply be Angel rather than an athlete under a microscope.Reese later made her position even clearer during another episode of, this time while speaking with Pretty Vee.“I think the next time I’ll post I’m in a relationship [on social media] is when I’m married,” Bayou Barbie said. “And that’s some time from now, so you ain’t gonna see it.”She followed that statement with another playful warning for anyone hoping to catch a glimpse of her dating life.“You might see me on a date. You gonna have to catch me though,” she continued. “Like, I’m not gonna post a man on my page.”A few days later, Reese reinforced the message herself.“The next time I’ll post in a relationship is when I’m married,” Reese wrote.Her stance makes sense in an era when a single photo can trigger days of speculation. For high-profile athletes, dating rumors can quickly become headlines, fan debates and social media arguments. Reese has experienced that attention firsthand, so choosing not to feed it gives her greater control over her personal life.Ironically, her relationship with Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. later became widely known despite her earlier promise. Rumors about the pair began circulating in early 2025, before Carter appeared at Reese’s birthday celebration and supported her courtside later that year.That does not necessarily erase the point Reese was making. Her comments were about refusing to turn a relationship into regular social media content.Reese's career has only made that boundary more important. As a first overall pick, three-time All-Star and one of the WNBA's most closely followed young stars, she knows almost every part of her life can become public conversation.Her solution is refreshingly direct. Fans can watch her compete, follow her career and celebrate her achievements. Her romantic life, however, does not have to become another performance.And if Reese stays true to the promise she made, the next relationship announcement may come with a very different title attached to it: husband.

Reese explained that the intense attention surrounding her dating life changed the way she views romance in the public eye. Her stance makes sense in an era when a single photo can trigger days of speculation.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million; after more than 18 months on the market, it fell to $6.7 million
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million; after more than 18 months on the market, it fell to $6.7 million

What does Cristiano Ronaldo’s 23-acre Cheshire estate include

Why did Cristiano Ronaldo leave the Cheshire mansion after returning to Manchester United

Why was Cristiano Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate listed for sale in 2023

Why did Cristiano Ronaldo’s property price fall to $6.7 million

$6.7 million

How did Cristiano Ronaldo’s earlier Cheshire home perform when he sold it

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Cheshire estate was listed for about $7.4 million in 2023, but the asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million after the property struggled to find a buyer. The huge estate in Alderley Edge covers 23 acres and includes a seven-bedroom mansion, six bathrooms, an indoor heated pool, gym, sauna, jacuzzi and cinema. There are also tennis and padel courts and a separate two-bedroom guest barn. Ronaldo moved into the property after returning to Manchester United in 2021, but his family soon moved to another Cheshire home. The estate was later put up for sale after his move to Saudi Arabia.Ronaldo’s former Cheshire home is built on a scale that goes well beyond a typical luxury house. The estate covers 23 acres in Alderley Edge, one of the well-known wealthy areas in Cheshire, while the main mansion has seven bedrooms and six bathrooms.The house was designed with both family life and fitness in mind. The main bedroom has private dressing areas and walk-in wardrobe space, while the other bedrooms have en-suite facilities.A large leisure area is one of the biggest features of the property. It has an indoor heated swimming pool, sauna and jacuzzi, along with a professional gym. For entertainment, there is a private cinema room and a wine cellar.The outdoor space adds even more to the property. Ronaldo’s former estate has a full-sized tennis court and a padel court, giving the owner options for sport without leaving the grounds.There is also a separate two-bedroom guest barn. It provides additional space for visitors, staff or security personnel while keeping the main house private.When Jackson-Stops listed the property, the estate agency described it as a “masterpiece of modern design set in 23 acres - an ultra stylish main residence with superb leisure suite, two bedroom guest barn and padel court.”Ronaldo did not stay in the mansion for long after returning to Manchester United in 2021. He and his family moved out soon after arriving in the area and shifted to another property in Cheshire.One explanation that appeared in reports at the time involved the land around the house. The estate bordered open farmland, and early-morning noise from sheep was said to have been a problem for Ronaldo.However, that detail has been disputed and should not be treated as the confirmed reason for the move. Privacy and security were also reported as concerns, especially because a public footpath ran close to the property.For someone as well known as Ronaldo, having people regularly passing near the estate could make privacy harder to maintain. His family therefore moved to another Cheshire property that had previously been owned by former Manchester United striker Andrew Cole.That home offered stronger security measures, including electric gates and CCTV, making it a better fit for the family.Ronaldo’s second Manchester United spell ended in November 2022 after his contract was terminated by mutual consent. The decision followed his high-profile television interview with Piers Morgan, in which he openly criticized the club and its leadership.A few weeks later, Ronaldo began the next stage of his career in Saudi Arabia after signing for Al-Nassr. That move also changed where he and his family spent most of their time.With Ronaldo no longer playing in Manchester, keeping a 23-acre estate in Cheshire made less sense. The property had already not been his family’s main home during the latter part of his United spell.Jackson-Stops placed the estate on the market in February 2023 with an asking price of £5.5 million, which was about $7.4 million based on the conversion used for the listing.The sale came as Ronaldo’s property holdings continued to stretch across several countries. Rather than keeping a large home in northern England that he was no longer using, the Cheshire estate became a property he could sell.Finding a buyer for a property of this size can take time. Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate remained on the market for more than 18 months, and the asking price was eventually reduced by £500,000.The new guide price was £5 million, or aboutThe reduction does not mean the property was sold for $6.7 million. It was the lower asking price after the original listing failed to attract a buyer within the expected period.There are practical reasons why a property like this can take longer to sell. The estate has 23 acres of land, which means a buyer is taking on much more than the upkeep of a normal house. The mansion also has a long list of specialist facilities, including an indoor pool, gym, tennis court and padel court.Those features can be attractive to the right buyer, but they can also make the property more expensive and demanding to maintain.The price cut also stands out because Ronaldo has previously experienced a difficult sale in the same area.Ronaldo owned another house in Alderley Edge during his first Manchester United spell. That property was a five-bedroom brick house with luxury facilities, including an indoor swimming pool and gym.He bought the earlier property in 2008 for a reported £3.895 million. It was eventually sold in 2019 for £3.25 million, meaning the sale price was around £645,000 lower than what he had originally paid.That house and the current 23-acre estate are different properties, but both show that even a famous footballer’s luxury home can take time to sell.The current estate was bought around Ronaldo’s return to Manchester United and later became unnecessary after his career moved away from England. Its large size and unusual collection of facilities also put it into a small section of the property market.For now, the important change is the asking price. Ronaldo’s former seven-bedroom Cheshire estate went from about $7.4 million to $6.7 million, but a final sale price has not been confirmed.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million in 2023. The asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million after the property struggled to find a buyer. Ronaldo moved into the property after returning to Manchester United in 2021, but his family soon moved to another Cheshire home. The estate was later put up for sale after his move to Saudi Arabia.

Jonathan Kuminga has finally made his choice after entering NBA free agency with several teams interested in his services. The newly minted Minnesota Timberwolves star chose Anthony Edwards ’ team over the Los Angeles Lakers, even though reports indicated Los Angeles was prepared to offer him more money. For Kuminga, the appeal was less about the biggest contract and more about finding the right place to win. His decision also gives him a chance to join a young Minnesota group with high expectations for the upcoming season.Kuminga explained his thinking during his introductory press conference in Minnesota, pointing to the Timberwolves’ recent success and the atmosphere around the franchise. The 23-year-old also spoke about his desire to help the team win while keeping his attention on the present rather than making predictions about his long-term future.The Timberwolves agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with Kuminga this offseason, according to ESPN. The contract includes a $6.3 million player option for the second season, giving him an important decision after the upcoming campaign.Kuminga could enter free agency again next offseason or choose to return for the 2026-27 NBA season. Much will depend on how his first year in Minnesota goes and how well he fits alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert.The move gives Minnesota an NBA champion who already has significant experience despite being only 23. His agent, Aaron Turner, said Kuminga had a clear preference after considering his options.Kuminga had several suitors during free agency, with the Lakers among the teams reportedly competing most seriously for him. Chicago and Portland were also listed among his other options.The decision to choose Minnesota became more notable because Kuminga reportedly turned down more lucrative opportunities. A one-year structure within the deal also gives him a path back to free agency, but Kuminga focused on something else when asked about his choice."I think this was the best decision for me," he said. "I just wanted to go to a winning culture. I think this was one of the best winning cultures I could have chose out of all the options. I spoke to so many people on this team, including front office, coaches, some of the players, and the vibe was just the type of vibe I was looking for."Minnesota has built a strong recent record under Tim Connelly and Chris Finch. The Timberwolves have made five straight playoff appearances and won at least one series in three consecutive seasons, including two trips to the Western Conference finals.Over the past three seasons, Minnesota has gone 154-92 with 24 playoff wins. The Lakers have gone 150-96 during the same span but have six playoff victories. Kuminga's decision, therefore, reflects the current direction of the two teams rather than their historic resumes."I would say it's one of the best decisions I've made, just looking at the roster, looking at the young group of guys they have," Kuminga said. "Seeing what they've done in the past and things they're trying to accomplish going forward. I think I fit well with this culture and I can come here and help win as many games as we can."I think the choice was, we're trying to win. Trying to help winning. That's why I made this decision."Kuminga also offered an early glimpse at what excites him about his new teammates, particularly Ball. The Timberwolves added the star guard via a trade with the Charlotte Hornets, and Kuminga said he was impressed by Ball's passing during a workout.“I was watching him work out yesterday. I was watching him doing certain things, and just the way he passed the ball, it’s incredible,” Kuminga said of Ball. “I mean, I’ve played with so many point guards in my career, but I never played with somebody that could pass as good as LaMelo. So, I think I’m looking forward to it, and I’m excited.”Kuminga previously played with elite point guards Chris Paul and Stephen Curry, making his praise for Ball notable. His comment also adds another layer to the expectations surrounding Minnesota after an active offseason.For now, Kuminga is focused on making the most of his opportunity. He was asked about staying with the Timberwolves beyond the upcoming season, but he avoided looking too far ahead.
Article Summary: Jonathan Kuminga chose the Minnesota Timberwolves over the Los Angeles Lakers. The 23-year-old agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Timberwolves. The contract includes a $6.3 million player option for the second season. Minnesota has made five straight playoff appearances.

Article Title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s fiancé Georgios Frangulis built his own empire before becoming her biggest supporter
Article Text:
Georgios Frangulis and Aryna Sabalenka (Getty Images)

Who is Georgios Frangulis, Aryna Sabalenka 's fiancé?

Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis (Getty Images)

How did Georgios Frangulis build Oakberry into a global brand?

When did Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis start dating?

How did Georgios Frangulis propose to Aryna Sabalenka?

What is 'The Gride,' Georgios Frangulis's new fashion brand?

Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores across 50 countries. Now 37, Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026, capping a relationship that began when she signed on as an Oakberry brand ambassador in early 2024.Born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil, Frangulis has Greek roots, with his family originally from Thessaloniki, Greece. He studied law at FAAP -- Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado -- in 2014, but never sat the bar exam."I always knew I wouldn't be a lawyer," he said. "What I really wanted was to be an entrepreneur."That clarity of purpose was rare at the time. Most people spend years hedging. Frangulis walked away from a law degree, moved to the United States, where he became infatuated with açaí, came back to São Paulo, and launched Oakberry in December 2016.Co-founded alongside Renato Haidar, Oakberry was not just another smoothie shop. Frangulis positioned açaí as functional nutrition -- clean ingredients, no artificial syrups, and a strong link to fitness culture -- and built a franchise model designed from day one to scale internationally.The company raised $67 million in capital in late 2023. By mid-2026, Oakberry had grown to a 900-location global business, with stores in Dubai malls, Miami gyms, Australian beach towns, and European city centres -- all without compromising brand consistency.In June 2023, Frangulis graced the cover of Forbes Brazil. The profile explored not just his entrepreneurial arc but his spirituality and Greek identity. His bicep tattoo reads "Fight for us, Saint George the Warrior." His forearm reads, "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." These are not the accessories of a brand persona.His net worth in 2026 is estimated between $75 million and $100 million -- built almost entirely from his equity in Oakberry, not from market listings or quick exits.They met in January 2024 when Sabalenka was hired as an ambassador for Oakberry. The couple were first spotted together in April 2024 -- a month after the tragic and untimely death of Sabalenka's ex-boyfriend, Konstantin Koltsov, who died by suicide in March 2024.It was a difficult period, and Sabalenka has been open about what Frangulis meant to her during it. "There was a really tough period where I was really happy to have him by my side, always cheering me up, always making sure that we are doing some fun stuff," she told People. "His support means so much to me. Being on the road and having him support me, to make me laugh and to be able to work out together, makes life on the road feel more like home. "Sabalenka had been broadly hinting for months. After winning the Brisbane International in January 2026, she said in her victory speech: "Thank you to my boyfriend... Hopefully soon I can call you something else, right? Let's just put some extra pressure."Frangulis proposed to Sabalenka in Indian Wells, California, on March 3, 2026. The setting was candlelit, with rose petals arranged beside a pool -- a rental home the couple had spent time in since the early days of their relationship. Sabalenka, in jeans and a white t-shirt, had no idea it was coming."I always knew I wanted to propose to Aryna because I was 100% sure she was the person I wanted to spend the rest of my life with," he shared in a YouTube video about the moment.The ring was designed by Isabela Grutman, who worked with Frangulis for months to create the custom piece. It features a 12-carat, oval-cut diamond surrounded by emeralds set in platinum -- Sabalenka's favorite stone, and also her birthstone. Experts told InStyle the ring could be worth up to $1 million. They captioned their joint Instagram post: "You & me, forever."Earlier in 2026, Frangulis launched his own fashion brand, named The Gride. The name honors his Greek heritage and mixes the words Greek and Pride. "My pride comes from my grandparents and has spread to my closest circle," the brand's website states. "The feeling is unmatched, and I'll do my best to make each and every one of you feel it too."Outside business, Frangulis races Porsche GT3 Cup cars. "Getting in the car and racing is one of the few moments when nothing else matters," he told Forbes Brazil. For someone whose professional life spans dozens of countries and time zones, that says something about how he recharges.What is clear is that Frangulis arrived in this relationship with his own story already written. He built a global company from a fruit most of the world had never heard of, then quietly showed up for the woman he loves at every stop on the tour. That is not a supporting role. It is just a different kind of ambition.
Article Summary: Georgios Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business. He is estimated to be worth between $75 million and $100 million.

Article Title: “When someone has an argument...": How Aaron Rodgers’ friendship with Mina Kimes fell apart after his controversial views changed their friendship
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers reveals why his friendship with Mina Kimes ended (Getty Images)

What exactly did Aaron Rodgers say about Mina Kimes?

Why did Aaron Rodgers say he used the word "immunized" in 2021?

How did Mina Kimes respond to Rodgers' comments?

What does this say about Rodgers heading into the 2026 season?

Aaron Rodgers has never been shy about speaking his mind, but his appearance on the *Not Just Football with Cam Heyward* podcast on September 10 crossed from opinion into something more personal. The 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback called out NFL analyst Mina Kimes by name, claiming she was among the media friends who turned on him after he spoke out against COVID vaccinations. What followed was a candid, at times sharp, account of how one decision reshaped nearly every professional relationship he had built in the media.Aaron Rodgers made it clear that the fallout was not limited to Kimes alone. He recalled a time when the media genuinely valued his perspective — on Colin Kaepernick, on social issues, even on moments that earned him a handwritten note from President Obama. "Everybody loved hearing my takes," he said. "Mina Kimes had me to her house for a feature I did. All of these people were my friends in the media. Until I came out against COVID. "That line carries a lot of weight. Rodgers is not just describing a friendship that faded.He is describing a pattern — a conditional kind of acceptance that disappeared the moment his views became inconvenient.He pushed back on the criticism that followed, arguing that his critics abandoned facts for personal attacks. "When someone has an argument and all they can ever say is, they attack your character instead of the content of what you're actually saying, you know that you're actually on the right side of things," he said.This is where Rodgers gets into territory he has revisited multiple times over the years. He explained that his use of the word "immunized" was tied to an active appeal he was making to the NFL regarding his vaccination status. "When I said I was immunized, it was because that statement alone was the crux of my entire argument and ongoing appeal with the NFL around my vaccination status," he said on the podcast.Rodgers later admitted he had avoided the vaccines due to an allergy to polyethylene glycol and expressed skepticism about the Johnson and Johnson vaccine. His appeal to the NFL, which sought to have treatment from a holistic doctor count toward his vaccination status, was ultimately denied.Beyond the semantics, Rodgers says the bigger issue was how unvaccinated players were treated inside team facilities. "Not to mention the hypocrisy around the treatment of players that were non-vaxxed, the inhumane way that we were treated as secondhand citizens around the facility, the way that we couldn't do anything on the road," he said.Kimes addressed Rodgers' vaccination controversy just two days earlier, on September 8, during an appearance on *The Sports Gossip Show*. "It was interesting to see him rehash the COVID stuff," she said. "He clearly was very bothered by the criticism."Kimes was careful to separate the issue. Her criticism, she said, was never about Rodgers being unvaccinated. "The criticism was that he lied about it by omission or whatever," she explained. She also pointed to Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins, who similarly pushed back against the vaccine but largely avoided the same level of media scrutiny. "I think those two are an interesting point of comparison," she added.That comparison is pointed. It suggests the media's response to Rodgers was not purely about vaccine hesitancy but about the specific way he handled the truth around it.Rodgers also called Fauci "an absolute, in my opinion, criminal," adding that people -- especially Black Americans -- should have "a healthy skepticism" toward government health agencies.His comments landed just days before his first game of the 2026 season, with the Steelers set to host the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium. At 42, Rodgers is likely in his final NFL season. And yet, rather than stepping back from controversy, he is leaning into it -- revisiting old grievances with the same conviction that created them in the first place.Whether you agree with him or not, the Rodgers-Kimes story is really a story about how COVID permanently rewired sports media relationships and drew lines that, five years later, have never fully moved.
Article Summary: Aaron Rodgers says Mina Kimes was among the media friends who turned on him after he spoke out against COVID vaccinations. Kimes says her criticism was that he lied about it by omission. Rodgers later admitted he had avoided the vaccines due to an allergy to polyethylene glycol.

Article Title: 'Won't take a lot for Gukesh to sow doubts in Javokhir Sindarov’s mind': Magnus Carlsen
Article Text:
Magnus Carlsen (Image credit: X)
