BENGALURU: World No. 1 and five-time world chess champion Magnus Carlsen has rated Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov as the favourite for his title match against incumbent D Gukesh. The face-off starts in Geneva on Nov 24.“Chess is a highly psychological sport, so probably it won’t take a lot to — potentially — put some doubts in Sindarov’s mind and gain some confidence along the way,” Carlsen told reporters here after his team Alpine APL Pipers went down 4-12 to Ganges Grandmasters in the Global Chess League on Thursday.“But as it stands, there’s no question that Sindarov is ahead. However, if you think that a certain match is an 80:20 at the start, the likelihood is still very high that it’s going to be a one-or-two score match (number of decisive games from the 14) because chess is such a drawish game. And that means that Gukesh (has a chance). He has shown that his ceiling is on par with or better than Sindarov’s. And it’s a short match. The first few games can determine a lot. If Sindarov is ahead early on, it would probably be very, very bad news (for the Indian fans). If he is ahead early on, he automatically becomes a significant favourite. That’s how these matches work,” added the Norwegian superstar.He minced no words when he said that assessing everything on the first few games of the match is incorrect.“It’s one of the reasons why I believe it’s an extraordinarily bad way to determine the best player in the world— you play classical, which is the most egalitarian format, but you don’t play a ton of games as well,” he said.Carlsen also said that Gukesh should not be in a position where he has to “defend everything”.“The word ‘defend’ is already adding pressure (being the defending champ). It’s not a good place to begin with, going by the way Gukesh has played for the last couple of years. He should be in a position where he has everything to gain. He has shown in 2024 that when things click, he has the potential to play at an extremely high level.“While many people don’t believe he will succeed now, it’s a more interesting challenge for him to try and regain that level.”Though Carlsen had withdrawn from the World Championship cycle before the 2023 match (Ding Liren vs Ian Nepomniachtchi), he is the reigning world champion in three other FIDE events — freestyle, rapid & blitz. He is also expected to play the inaugural Total Chess World Championship tour next year, a joint venture between Norway chess organisers and FIDE that combined various time controls under one umbrella.The top-2 players from that tour will qualify for the 2028 Candidates tournament.Does this window offer fans hope to see Carlsen vs Gukesh or Sindarov matchup for the Classical World Championship? Carlsen, 35, made his disinterest clear.“If anything has changed, it’s kind of the other way (losing more interest).”Results (Day 6): APL Pipers 4 lost to Ganges 12, Triveni 5 lost to Mumba 14, Pipers 11 bt Knights 6, Gambits 13 bt Ganges 5.
Article Summary: Magnus Carlsen has rated Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov as the favourite for his title match against incumbent D Gukesh. The face-off starts in Geneva on Nov 24. “Chess is a highly psychological sport, so probably it won’t take a lot to — potentially — put some doubts in Sindarov’s mind and gain some confidence along the way,” Carlsen said.

Article Title: “Need some luck”: George Russell breaks silence on Kimi Antonelli and reveals why his F1 title fight has become so tough
Article Text:
George Russell admits he may need luck to keep his F1 title hopes alive (Image via IG/X)

George Russell gives Kimi Antonelli credit while refusing to walk away from the title fight

George Russell faces a fresh challenge at the new Madrid circuit with Kimi Antonelli ahead

George Russell is refusing to pretend that the Formula 1 championship battle is closer than it looks. With Kimi Antonelli holding a 66-point advantage, the Mercedes driver has admitted that his team mate has been the stronger performer so far this season. Russell still has his eyes on the title, but he knows the numbers are not in his favor. Antonelli arrives at the Spanish Grand Prix after another big win at Monza, while Russell is looking for a response. The Briton believes his recent form has improved, but he also accepts that something extra may be needed if he is to turn the championship around.The gap between the two Mercedes drivers has become one of the biggest stories of the 2026 season. Russell made a strong start to the year, but Antonelli has gradually taken control of the championship with a remarkable run of results.The Italian has now won seven races, including a dramatic comeback at Monza after starting 19th. Russell finished second in Italy, but he could not prevent his team mate from taking another major step toward the title.Russell was direct when assessing the situation.“I'm not trying to be delusional, the reality is my team mate has done a better job than me this year.Had some bad luck but he deserves to be leading and right now he deserves to be in the position he is.“From my side, I'm just going race by race, going to try and win as many as possible. If I want to win this championship I'm going to need some luck and that's where we are. I'm being quite realistic about the position we're in.”That honesty does not mean Russell has given up. His focus is now on getting the most out of every race rather than worrying about the championship standings.He also praised Antonelli's consistency, pointing out that the 19-year-old has not suffered a bad weekend in terms of performance. That level of form has made Russell's task even harder.The Spanish Grand Prix presents a different challenge because the Madring circuit in Madrid is new to Formula 1. Drivers have limited experience of the layout, meaning confidence and adaptability could play a major role.Russell believes the circuit will demand plenty from the drivers, particularly through its high-speed sections and aggressive kerbs.“The level of everyone in F1 is exceptionally high,” he said. “It’s going to be a circuit where you need confidence.“Very challenging, lots of high speed corners, aggressive kerbs. Going to be an experience for sure. Just try and keep out of the wall and build up to it.“Every race is an opportunity. This circuit is among the most risky circuits of the season. You want to put everything on the line and go for pole and victory but how I approach this race, it's just going about business as usual.”That mindset could be important for Russell. The championship deficit is significant, but there are still races remaining and opportunities to collect points.For now, Russell appears more interested in finding speed than calculating the title standings. Antonelli has the advantage, but the Mercedes driver knows the championship can change quickly in Formula 1.His task is clear. He needs to keep improving, win as many races as possible and hope the luck he has been missing this season eventually arrives.
Article Summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the Formula 1 championship by 66 points from George Russell. The Italian has won seven races this season, including a dramatic comeback at Monza. Russell admits he may need luck to keep his title hopes alive. The Mercedes driver has praised his team mate's consistency this season.

The kid in our team (Vaibhav Sooryavanshi) is literally as old as my career. He has that youthful innocence, loves to joke around, and absorbs things quickly,” Shami said.The 36-year-old believes the exposure young players receive today, particularly through the IPL and other high-pressure competitions, has accelerated their development.“But most of these youngsters are already quite mature. With the level of cricket they play today—featuring in the IPL and other high-pressure tournaments—maturity comes early, so you don't need to over-coach them,” he said.“But yes, when the game gets tight and challenging, that's when you step in with tactical inputs and remind them to keep fighting,” he added.“There are plenty of reasons to stay motivated if you look for them. At this level, if you aren't self-motivated, your approach is wrong. No matter what stage you’re playing at, your eyes must always be set on the next level,” he said.Shami took two important wickets, dismissing Ravichandran Smaran and Sheikh Rasheed, as East Zone secured the Duleep Trophy title on the basis of a first-innings lead. The triumph also coincided with his 100th first-class appearance.“As far as satisfaction goes, achieving this in my 100th match—and that too in a winning Duleep Trophy final—is special. East Zone has won this after a very long time. You’ve seen how we performed.“Every single boy put his heart and soul into this campaign to get us here. To achieve this in these conditions, in this heat, is outstanding. As for me, whether it’s your first match or your 100th, it doesn’t matter—the effort and the approach remain exactly the same,” he said.Shami also stressed that the level of cricket does not change his approach.“When you wear that crest on your chest, the level of cricket doesn't matter. If you play for the badge, that hunger will naturally show. Your willingness to fight only grows when you play with that pride.“My mindset is simple: whichever level I get an opportunity to play, I want to make it count and fulfil my responsibility toward the team,” he said.
Article Summary: Mohammed Shami believes young Indian cricketers are arriving with a level of maturity that means they need less coaching and more timely guidance. Shami has not played for India since March 2025 and last featured in a Test during the World Test Championship final against Australia at The Oval in 2023. The 36-year-old believes the exposure young players receive today, particularly through the IPL and other high-pressure competitions, has accelerated their development.

Article Title: Delhi HC denies Vinesh Phogat entry to World Championships trials: ‘Not inclined to grant interim exemption’
Article Text:
Vinesh Phogat

Phogat challenges September 7 WFI circular

Court had sought WFI, Centre response

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to allow wrestler Vinesh Phogat to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships, declining her request for an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI).Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma, in a late-night interim order, said that at this stage, the court was not inclined to grant an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria to allow Phogat to participate in the selection trials on September 14.“To reiterate, the criteria prescribed under the circular dated September 7, 2026 apply uniformly to all athletes. An athlete who has not participated in the prescribed competitions, for whatever reason, would not fall within the eligibility categories specified by respondent no. 1 (WFI),” the court said.The high court passed the order while dismissing an application by Phogat, who has returned from maternity leave, seeking permission to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships.Court flags Phogat’s maternity circumstancesThe court said Phogat’s circumstances relating to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum recovery would require consideration while examining the validity of the policy.However, that does not, at the interim stage, by itself entitle her to a direction permitting her to participate contrary to the eligibility criteria, it added.“Granting such interim relief to the petitioner alone, without first adjudicating upon the policy itself, may consequently result in unequal treatment of similarly situated athletes who are not before this court,” it said.The court added that without expressing any final opinion on the validity of the circular or on the merits of the pending disciplinary proceedings, it was not inclined to grant the interim relief.Phogat, in her application filed in a pending petition, had also sought a stay on the operation of a September 7 circular issued by the WFI prescribing the eligibility criteria for the selection trials scheduled for September 14 at the Indira Gandhi Stadium here.The fresh application was filed in the main petition in which Phogat has sought formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.In the application, she sought a stay on the circular as it excludes her from participating in the selection trials for the championship scheduled to be held at Astana, Kazakhstan from October 24 to November 1.The WFI circular provides for women’s trials in six Olympic weight categories. Phogat contended that the latest selection framework creates a closed pathway by making eligibility dependent on participation and performance in specified qualifying competitions.The plea said the circular places Phogat in a position where she is excluded not because she has been assessed and found wanting on sporting merit but because she was unable to participate in the particular competitions selected by WFI as gateways to the present selection trials.It said the framework contains no mechanism to account for an athlete who was unable to participate in the prescribed competitions for maternity-related reasons.On September 1, the high court sought the response of WFI and the Centre on Phogat’s plea seeking formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.In the petition, she has sought directions for formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning from maternity, transparent and objectively verifiable selection and nomination processes, and an alternative mechanism for athletes disadvantaged by maternity-related absence.Phogat, who became a mother in July 2025, said upon resuming her wrestling career after childbirth, she was made to re-enter the competitive pathway without any accommodation for the period she was unable to compete due to maternity.The wrestler has also filed another petition seeking quashing of two show cause notices issued to her by the WFI and disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.WFI’s counsel had said they kept the hearing twice but “there has been no show”; a final opportunity was given and the hearing was on September 2.In the plea, Phogat said that the two notices issued to her on May 9 and June 17 were part of a continuing pattern of arbitrary and mala fide action by the WFI, obstructing her return to competitive wrestling after maternity.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to allow wrestler Vinesh Phogat to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships. The court declined her request for an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI)

CHENNAI: At 36, Mohammed Shami may have a century of First-class matches under his belt, but the hunger remains the same.As East Zone ended a 14-year wait to win their third Duleep Trophy, it was the veteran pacer’s third Duleep title as well.“Achieving this in my 100th match is special. Article Title: New York Yankees rookie Spencer Jones reveals what makes Aaron Judge so special and why his advice means so much
Article Text:
Spencer Jones opens up about the mentor who has helped shape his Yankees journey (Image via IG/X)

Spencer Jones explains why Aaron Judge has been such an important mentor

Yankees fans can now see why the Jones and Judge pairing matters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Spencer Jones has spent years watching Aaron Judge from a distance. Now, the New York Yankees rookie is getting the chance to learn from the superstar up close, and he clearly understands how valuable that opportunity is. Jones recently shared an honest view of Judge, pointing to the veteran’s willingness to help and explain the thinking behind his game. For a young player trying to establish himself in the majors, having someone like Judge in the same clubhouse can make a real difference. Jones’ comments also give fans a closer look at the relationship developing between two Yankees outfielders as New York heads toward the postseason.Jones’ praise for Judge was not simply about the Yankees captain’s production on the field. Instead, he focused on the way Judge interacts with younger players and makes himself available when they need guidance.Judge has been around Jones since the rookie was selected in the first round of the 2022 MLB Draft. Over the years, that connection has grown, with Judge asking Jones questions and offering advice about different parts of the game.For Jones, that experience has become even more valuable now that both players are sharing a Yankees clubhouse and dugout.“Judge has been incredible. I think since I’ve been drafted, he’s been around. He’s been probing me, asking me questions. I think what’s so great about him is that there’s no guesswork to what he does. He’s got a reason behind a lot of things. He’s got opinions. He wants to help. And for a young player, it doesn’t get much better than that. Just as far as somebody who’s my size and plays a position that I do, and just being able to literally ask the greatest hitter of the last however many years certain questions about a swing or an approach or how to navigate, where to go to dinner, all of these things. This guy is in everybody’s corner here, and he’s been in mine for the last handful of years, and more so now that we’re sharing a dugout together. Yeah, he’s been a very incredible mentor, and I’m excited to keep working with him.”The quote shows why Jones values Judge beyond his status as one of baseball’s biggest stars. The rookie can ask him about hitting, preparation and the smaller details that come with playing in the majors.That access can be difficult for a young player to find, especially when the person offering advice has already experienced the pressure that comes with being the face of the Yankees.Jones made his MLB debut this season and has become part of the Yankees’ plans during an important stretch of the year. His development is now happening alongside Judge, giving the young outfielder a rare opportunity to learn from one of the best hitters of his generation.The timing is also important for New York.Judge recently returned to the lineup after missing 84 games because of a rib stress fracture. His return gives the Yankees another major offensive weapon as they fight for position in the American League and prepare for the postseason.Jones has given the team reasons to remain interested in his development, too. Through 72 games, he was batting .245 with a .326 on-base percentage and a .446 slugging percentage. He had also hit nine home runs and driven in 31 runs.Fans are especially excited about seeing Jones and Judge share the outfield. The idea of the established superstar working alongside a promising young player has added another layer to the Yankees’ late-season story.MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM captured the relationship with a simple line: “Almost everyone looks up to Aaron Judge, literally. Spencer Jones looks up to him, figuratively.”That reaction says plenty about how Judge is viewed inside and outside the Yankees clubhouse. But Jones’ comments show there is more to the relationship than admiration.For the rookie, Judge is someone he can turn to with questions, someone who explains the reasons behind his approach and someone who wants younger players to succeed.As the Yankees push toward October, that kind of connection could become increasingly valuable. Jones is still learning what it takes to thrive in the majors, and he has one of baseball’s biggest stars close by to help him figure it out.
Article Summary: Spencer Jones says Aaron Judge has been a mentor to him since he was drafted. The Yankees rookie says Judge is willing to help and explain the thinking behind his game. Jones' comments give fans a closer look at the relationship between the two players.

Article Title: “Can they get any more disrespectful?”: LA Clippers wrapped in another ugly controversy after Chris Paul decision who played 21 years in NBA
Article Text:
Chris Paul. Image via: Getty Images

Clippers make bold roster call despite promise made to Chris Paul

Bradley Beal responds to Clippers controversy over Chris Paul

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NBA fans react to Clippers controversy

The Los Angeles Clippers have picked a fresh fight with their own history. Chris Paul's old No. 3, the number he wore for six seasons that turned the franchise into a real playoff team, is heading to Bradley Beal for the coming season.The decision lands on an organization already reeling from the league's punishment in the Kawhi Leonard cap circumvention case, and it has reopened a wound from Paul's messy exit last season. Beal has responded publicly, but the backlash from fans hasn't slowed down.NBA reporter Etienne Catalan first flagged the move this week. With Beal returning to the Clippers for the 2026-27 season, the team plans to give him Paul's old No. 3, a number the Clippers' own team store has already listed for Beal heading into the year.That contradicts what Paul says he was told. Appearing on Carmelo Anthony's "7 PM in Brooklyn" podcast, Paul said the organization had promised to retire the number once he stepped away from the game. The Clippers have never retired a single jersey in their history, and Paul, who called his exit "most disrespectful," says the number now sitting on Beal's back is proof the team never meant to keep its word.The backdrop makes it worse. Paul spent six seasons building the Clippers into a perennial playoff team during his first stint, then returned for a second run in 2025 that ended badly. He was reportedly informed in the middle of the night that the team was moving on from him, then sent home in December amid claims he was undermining the coaching staff, a characterization he disputed.When Paul signed with the Clippers in 2025, Beal voluntarily gave up the No. 3 he had worn his entire career so Paul could keep the number tied to his "CP3" identity. Team president Lawrence Frank called it "such a great gesture" at the time, saying Beal wanted to hand over the number before Paul even knew about it.With that goodwill now looking undone, Beal took to social media to get ahead of the criticism. He called Paul "a legend," and added that his history and brand with the franchise could never be erased.The message reads less like a man trying to justify wearing the number and more like someone caught in the middle of a situation he didn't create.Fans weren't as forgiving. Reaction poured in across social media once the news about the 21-year NBA legend spread.@CKenzyNelson wrote: "We can't be mad at Bradley Beal for wearing No. 3 with the Los Angeles Clippers. The Clippers allowed him to wear it 🤷🏽‍♂️ For some reason, they seem to hate Chris Paul, even after everything he did for that franchise 🤦🏽‍♂️🏀"@cmonnowplayaman asked simply: "Why take the number then lmao"@CanyonDriver joked: "Revenge plot for CP3 if he's a GM for the Lakers. smoovay"@Slime5ea5on summed up the mood: "Can they get any more disrespectful lol"@crmnchin6969 didn't hold back: "clippers cant do anything right. will always be the lakers little bro"And @curgoat09 wasn't buying Beal's message either: "'He's a legend' still got that number on though"The Clippers can’t catch a break. After the Kawhi Leonard controversy, the team is now under fresh scrutiny.
Article Summary: Bradley Beal will wear Chris Paul's old No. 3 for the coming season. Paul says the team promised to retire the number once he left the game. The Clippers have never retired a single jersey in their history. Beal took to social media to respond to the criticism.

Just a day after the CM's wife opposed religious curbs on participation in garba events, she reached out to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange, describing him as her brother and inviting him home for a meal.Jarange, unrelenting in his criticism of Devendra Fadnavis amidst a hunger strike for Maratha quota, appeared restrained in his response. He said it was not the right time for him to visit the CM's residence. However, if the offer was intended with "affection and compassion", he would meet her during Bhaubeej, a festival after Diwali that celebrates the brother-sister bond. Jarange said he was determined to travel to Mumbai in coming days, but to press for his demands. He said he would spell out his plan on Sept 12. tnn & agenciesAmruta Fadnavis’s invitation to Jarange came as she spoke to reporters in Nagpur on Wednesday. Asked about the activist, she said, “Jarange Patilji is my brother, and I invite him for a meal at our home.”has been staging a hunger strike to demand reservation for the Maratha community under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. He has also been seeking issuance of Kunbi caste certificates to eligible members of the Maratha community.“If the brother is agitating, the sister should not call at this moment for food. The brother will have a problem. The sister should think about it and call me on Bhaubeej...will go with a saree (for her), and this is my word,” Jarange said on Thursday. He said if someone speaks with good intention, there is no need to question it every time.“If you are calling me from the battlefield, then I have to accept defeat. If someone is saying something with a good feeling, there is no need to take it otherwise. But this is not the time to go on her invitation because the brother is currently fighting for the kids of poor people,” he added.Asked about no govt representatives coming to meet him, Jarange said he did not wait for anyone in the past three years of his agitation. “I am agitating on my own capacity. The (govt) delegation will behave according to the way it is guided. It is okay when there is one guide. If guides from various thought schools come together, it creates a mess.”Reiterating his plan, Jarange said, “I am definitely going to Mumbai and will declare the date on Sept 12. Nothing will be hidden.”
Article Summary: Amruta Fadnavis’s invitation to Manoj Jarange came as she spoke to reporters in Nagpur. Jarange has been staging a hunger strike to demand reservation for the Maratha community under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. He said he would spell out his plan on Sept 12.

Article Title: Pune cops nab eatery owner, aide after 32km chase for abducting civil services aspirant
Article Text:
(AI image) An eatery owner and his accomplice were arrested for abducting a civil services aspirant.​​





PUNE: An eatery owner and one of his accomplices were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they forced a civil services aspirant (28) into an SUV barely 400m away from Perugate police chowkey around 12.30am for talking to the suspect’s female friend.Police said the suspects drove the aspirant around the city while beating him up then transferred him to another vehicle, before releasing him near Alka Talkies and trying to flee.High drama ensued as police chased the suspects’ SUVs for about 32km. They ultimately arrested eatery owner Sagar Ramesh Borade (32) and his aide Kishor Balasaheb Sawant (32) on the charge of abducting the civil services aspirant Prasad Suryavanshi. A case of abduction and assault has been registered against five people, including Borade’s female friend, who is also a civil services aspirant and close to Suryavanshi.Suryavanshi hails from Baramati and is currently staying in a hostel near Perugate.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone I) Krushikesh Rawale on Thursday afternoon said, “Borade hails from Walchandnagar and is currently staying in Pune city. His accomplice Sawant is from Malshiras in Solapur district.They were arrested around 2.30am. We are searching for their two accomplices.”He added, “Borade runs an eatery on Laxmi Road near Alka Talkies Chowk. The woman civil services aspirant visited Borade regularly and chatted with Suryavanshi, too. Borade did not like it. He told her and Suryavanshi not to talk to each other.”The woman aspirant and Suryavanshi continued talking to each other despite Borade’s warning. “The matter escalated on Wednesday evening and Borade asked the woman to reveal Suryavanshi’s location. After she disclosed his location, Borade and three other men reached the spot in an SUV. They beat up Suryavanshi and pushed him into the vehicle,” Rawale said.The suspects allegedly punched and slapped Suryavanshi inside the SUV. They first drove to Dandekar Bridge, then proceeded to Wadgaon Bridge on Sinhagad Road and shifted Suryavanshi to another vehicle. Then, they drove to Katraj Ghat section.In the meantime, one of Suryavanshi’s hostel mates called the police control room and informed personnel about the abduction. Police studied the vehicle’s registration number and identified its owner as Borade.“Our team then called Borade on his phone, but he did not answer. We tracked the location of his cellphone and a team started chasing the SUV on motorcycles,” the DCP said.The police team chased the SUV in which Suryavanshi was abducted and taken to the Sinhagad Road area, a distance of about 16km. The personnel chased the subsequent SUV also up to Alka Talkies Chowk, a distance of about another 16km. The police team on motorcycles again trailed the SUV as it started from Alka Talkies Chowk towards Swargate and finally intercepted it after a 1.5km chase. Borade and Sawant were then detained.
Article Summary: Sagar Ramesh Borade (32) and his aide Kishor Balasaheb Sawant ( 32) arrested on the charge of abducting the civil services aspirant Prasad Suryavanshi. High drama ensued as police chased the suspects’ SUVs for about 32km. A case of abduction and assault has been registered against five people, including Borade’s female friend.

Article Title: A demand to vacate house, trip to Delhi & murder in 15 minutes: How couple killed DU professor
Article Text:
A couple allegedly murdered a Delhi University professor over a property dispute in West Bengal.





NEW DELHI: A demand to vacate an ancestral property in West Bengal’s Bardhaman allegedly led a couple to hatch a plan to murder Delhi University professor Debosmita Paul at her residence in east Delhi’s Vasundhara Enclave in June, police have stated in their chargesheet.The couple allegedly took about 15 minutes to enter the society, kill Paul, change clothes and leave. The change of clothes, however, gave them away. Their young son, who was present at the spot, has been made a witness in the case.The chargesheet, filed in the first week of Sept, contains statements from more than 40 witnesses and runs into over 300 pages. The couple were booked for murder, criminal conspiracy, impersonation and other offences.Paul and her mother jointly owned an ancestral property spread over more than 1,000 square yards in Bardhaman. The accused couple had been living as tenants on the ground floor, with the rent deposited into Paul’s and her mother’s joint bank account. Paul had visited the property with her mother last year and told the couple they would have to vacate it. She initially asked them to leave by June and reiterated the demand on the phone in March this year.Police alleged that the husband, who works at a hardware shop, discussed the issue with his wife and they decided to kill Paul so they could continue living on the property. They allegedly believed other members of Paul’s family had little interest in the property and that they could eventually take control of it.The husband allegedly travelled to Delhi three times before the murder for a recce, observing Paul’s routine, residence and educational activities, the chargesheet states. On June 2, the couple travelled from Bardhaman to Delhi along with their son, aged 10, checked into a hotel, and allegedly carried out the murder the following day. They rang Paul’s doorbell, knowing she was familiar with them, and told her they had come to discuss the Bardhaman property. Once inside, they handed their young son a phone and went into another room.The accused allegedly attacked Paul on the head with a mortar before repeatedly striking her face and slitting both her wrists. Their son heard the commotion and entered the room, where he witnessed the incident, police said.Investigators said the entire sequence -- from the point the accused entered the society till they carried out the murder, changed clothes and then left -- took about 15 minutes. To evade detection, the duo allegedly changed their clothes at Paul’s house. They also used fake Aadhaar cards during their stay at the hotel.Police analysed footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras during the investigation. Footage from Paul’s society showed a masked couple entering around 3.20pm with a child and later leaving, with the two adults having changed clothes and the child still wearing the same clothes.Investigators questioned the cab driver who had dropped the family near Dallupura and traced their movements to the hotel where they had stayed. Hotel records showed the man was from Bihar and the woman from Bardhaman, prompting police to examine their links to the property.The couple was later traced to Anand Vihar. Instead of taking a train from there, they travelled to New Delhi railway station before boarding a train for Bardhaman. A police team reached Bardhaman, where investigators traced a scooter allegedly used by the accused, conducted door-to-door searches at more than 100 houses, and finally arrested the couple. The child was produced as a ‘child in need of care and protection’ before the Child Welfare Committee and his custody given to his relatives.
Article Summary: A couple allegedly murdered a Delhi University professor over a property dispute in West Bengal. The couple allegedly took about 15 minutes to enter the society, kill Paul, change clothes and leave. Their young son, who was present at the spot, has been made a witness in the case.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher who quit over AI safety walked away two months before his stock vested; says: I no longer have anything to gain by…
Article Text:
Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation.

Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch

Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

An Anthropic safety lead replied to the resignation thread and agreed with it

An Anthropic researcher who resigned this week over AI safety fears gave up his entire stake in the company to do it, walking out two months before his equity was due to vest.Jacob Coxon, 27, spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI before moving to Anthropic in July. He lasted four months. Staff need six for their stock to vest. His resignation post on X on September 9, now past 130 million views, said neither lab is acting responsibly and that both are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives".Axios first reported the forfeited equity, after Coxon told the outlet on Wednesday that "I no longer have anything to gain by juicing up Anthropic's valuation" and that he left before any of his shares vested. He still holds equity in OpenAI, where his work included GPT-4o.The company is preparing a listing at a reported $2 trillion valuation, built in large part on its reputation as the frontier lab that takes risk seriously. That is what gives the equity detail its weight. Researchers have walked out of rival labs over safety before, usually after their stock vested. Coxon left with nothing, then criticised the valuation he could have profited from.He drew that line carefully in the interview. Anthropic's safety work is sincere, he said, and he has not seen it compromised to outpace competitors. What worries him is pressure over time. Race hard enough and you cut corners, or skip steps in the oversight process. He also described a mood he thinks becomes self-fulfilling, calling it excessive paranoia about OpenAI and about China. Colleagues, he wrote earlier, have started using words like "crunchtime" and "endgame".His most quoted line was about where these decisions are being taken. It is insane, he said, that the work happens on the MacBooks of engineers in San Francisco rather than in a bunker in the desert like the Manhattan Project.Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress testing at Anthropic, wrote that he personally puts the odds of AI killing all humans above 10 percent within the decade. He said the company is trying, but has no plan yet for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to find one.Coxon's argument is partly about candour. Executives soften their phrasing for the press, he wrote, then say the same things privately, and the belief that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade is not a marketing stunt. He also described something that used to be a thought experiment. Models now know when they are being tested, and reason about the fact while it is happening.He pointed to the recent run of cyber incidents at frontier labs, including July's Hugging Face breach, as evidence the risk has left the theoretical stage. Coxon is among more than 1,000 researchers who recently signed a statement calling for governments to coordinate on a way to slow AI development if models start improving on their own. Anthropic has not commented on his departure.
Article Summary: Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation. Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch. Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.
